Description: A Kitchen conversation confirms the deceased is an outsider and cross-checks the number of people in the house, while creating a clear split: Harry Thornton goes to the Study to handle the scene, and Damian Maseko takes the drunken Doyle away to prevent further conflict.
Location: Kitchen (Kitchen)
Key Information:
  - Damian Maseko (No. 8) identifies himself and informs Harry Thornton that a death incident has occurred upstairs.
  - Harry Thornton confirms he heard the sound of a bottle shattering and decides to personally go to the Study (Study) to check.
  - Harry Thornton cross-checks the headcount: besides the two hosts, there are eight guests including Damian Maseko himself and Eve Dauer, plus Harry Thornton; the deceased is not among them.
  - Damian Maseko confirms the deceased is an outsider, consistent with his own judgment.
  - Harry Thornton asks Damian Maseko to look after the visibly drunken Eve Dauer and take her to Edmund Galley’s room (Edmund's room) to rest.
  - Harry Thornton reminds Damian Maseko to avoid the others as much as possible, especially Edmund Galley.
Characters:
  [Damian Maseko (Damian Maseko)] Person No. 8, one of the villa residents.
    · Notifies Harry Thornton about the upstairs death incident on Martha Galley’s orders.
    · Confirms the deceased is an outsider.
    · Looks after and takes the drunken Eve Dauer away at Harry Thornton’s request.
  [Harry Thornton (Harry Thornton)] Person No. 11, the villa’s butler.
    · Confirms hearing the bottle shattering sound.
    · Cross-checks the guest count and infers the deceased is not on the current list.
    · Decides to go to the Study (Study) to inspect and handle the scene.
    · Asks Damian Maseko to take Eve Dauer to Edmund Galley’s room (Edmund's room) to rest and warns him to avoid Edmund Galley.
  [Doyle] Person No. 10, a female resident who is visibly drunk or emotionally unstable.
    · Repeatedly questions the death news and shows confusion and unease.
    · Will be taken by Damian Maseko to Edmund Galley’s room (Edmund's room) to rest.
